Name: MermaidFlowchartRoutingIntentRuleset
Purpose: Golden ruleset for validating Mermaid flowchart recognition and routing intent generated from flow.md fixtures. This validates generic rule satisfaction, not exact SVG co-ordinates.

GenerationNotes: Scenario ids are fixtures only; rules must not special-case by scenario id at runtime.
RequiredGenericRuleIds identify the generic semantic/routing/rendering rules each fixture is expected to exercise.
SVG and pixel comparisons remain separate gates.

PassCondition: Every active fixture produces a diagram contract with all RequiredGenericRuleIds satisfied.
Every active fixture produces routing intent that avoids all listed ForbiddenBehaviours.
Remarked fixtures may be excluded from render gates but should still be recognised where Recognition rules are listed.
The renderer must report whether a failure is recognition, routing-intent, render-path, label-placement, or SVG-output related.

Normalise LR direction and apply primary horizontal routing expectations.
Normalise RL direction and invert primary horizontal entry/exit expectations.
Map symbolic direction tokens to canonical direction values.
Normalise TB/TD/top-down direction and apply primary vertical routing expectations.
Recognise flowchart as the flowchart diagram family.
Recognise flowchart-elk as flowchart with ELK renderer intent.
Recognise graph as flowchart-compatible input.
accTitle and accDescr are preserved as accessibility contract fields.
front-matter config is parsed and merged into effective config.
htmlLabels false changes label rendering mode to SVG/native text.
init directive is parsed before diagram recognition and affects effective config.
node/rank spacing overrides are preserved and affect layout expectations.
Node declarations before edges and declaration order differences do not change logical graph contract.
Animation metadata/style is recognised even when render output is excluded or downgraded.
Bidirectional markers are recognised without duplicating the logical edge.
Chained edge statements expand to separate logical edges.
Circle marker is recognised at the indicated edge end.
Cross marker is recognised at the indicated edge end.
Dotted edge stroke is recognised independently from marker style.
Ampersand grouped vertices expand to all required logical edges.
HTML edge label content is preserved and measured as label content.
Edge id on a grouped expansion applies only to the grammar-selected edge; other edges receive generated ids.
Invisible edge is recognised as a layout-affecting edge with hidden visual stroke.
Inline edge labels using -- text --> are preserved as edge labels.
Pipe-delimited edge labels are preserved as edge labels.
Long edge label is measured/wrapped without deriving minlen from label text.
Markdown-like edge label content is preserved and measured as label content.
Edge metadata mutates the identified edge contract.
Minlen is derived from link stroke length, not edge label width.
Explicit line breaks in edge labels are preserved for measurement and rendering.
Open line token produces an edge without point marker.
Point arrow marker is recognised independently from stroke style.
Thick edge stroke is recognised independently from marker style.
Edge token decomposes into stroke, marker start, marker end, directionality, and minlen.
User-defined edge id is preserved independently from endpoints.
click href/call interactions are recognised and emitted or diagnosed.
HTML label content is preserved for HTML label rendering and diagnostics.
Unlabelled vertex ids become visible labels without creating duplicate nodes.
Explicit line break intent is preserved in node labels.
Long labels require wrapping/measurement without changing node identity.
Markdown-like label content is preserved as label content requiring markdown/html handling.
Metadata label overrides default/id label and is preserved in the node contract.
Metadata shape data is preserved and mapped to canonical shape intent.
Quoted labels are preserved as string labels with outer quotes stripped.
Repeated vertex declarations merge into one node contract with deterministic effective properties.
Asymmetric flag syntax maps to asymmetric/flag shape intent.
Double-parentheses syntax maps to circle intent.
Cylinder syntax maps to database/cylinder intent.
Brace syntax maps to decision diamond intent.
Triple-parentheses syntax maps to double-circle intent.
Double-brace syntax maps to hexagon intent.
Bracket rectangle syntax maps to canonical rectangle intent.
Parenthesised node syntax maps to rounded rectangle intent.
Stadium/pill syntax maps to stadium shape intent.
Double-bracket syntax maps to subroutine/framed rectangle intent.
Legacy trapezoid/lean bracket syntax maps to canonical trapezoid or lean shape intent.
Unicode label text is accepted and preserved.
Mermaid %% comments are never model facts.
Semicolons and newlines are both recognised as statement boundaries.
class statement applies classes to comma-separated or listed targets.
classDef creates reusable class style contract.
Inline :::class syntax is captured during node recognition.
linkStyle/default interpolate mutates edge or default curve intent.
linkStyle creates indexed/default edge style mutation.
linkStyle default applies to all matching edges.
style directive mutates the target element style contract.
Bare subgraph title form is preserved.
Subgraph creates a group contract and membership list.
Edges crossing group boundaries are ordinary edges with group context.
Subgraph-local direction is captured on the group contract.
Explicit subgraph id and quoted title form is preserved.
Node has one effective parent group and nested ownership remains deterministic.
Nested groups preserve parent/child group ownership.
Curve intent is selected from edge metadata, linkStyle interpolation, front-matter, init, or default config.
HTML label mode uses foreignObject/HTML measurement expectations.
Markers are attached according to token decomposition and resolved style.
htmlLabels:false uses native SVG text measurement/rendering expectations.
Style/theme mutations are resolved before SVG comparison.
Adjacent-rank primary-flow edges should use primary centre exit/entry and avoid unnecessary detours.
Back/return edges should route around the primary flow without crossing node bodies.
ELK scenarios use ELK layout/routing intent rather than Dagre-only assumptions.
Many-to-one routing should merge cleanly at a target without ambiguous visual collapse.
One-to-many routing should distribute branches without collapsing unrelated paths.
Invisible edges affect layout but do not render visible stroke or marker.
Edge labels require clearance and must remain visually attached to the owning edge.
Decision branches should leave from distinct appropriate boundary regions and keep labels attached to branches.
Long labels require wrapping/clearance without causing excessive detours or minlen changes.
Parallel or branch paths merging back to a downstream node should form clear merge-back routes.
Extra-hyphen minlen edges may span ranks using dummy segments while snapping endpoints to real nodes.
Nodes with multiple incoming edges require distinct entry handling and collision avoidance.
Multiple decision branches should fan out without branch/label ambiguity.
Nested subgraph routing must respect inner and outer group boundaries and directions.
Edges must avoid unrelated node bodies and cluster bodies.
Orthogonal routing expects axis-aligned segments with legal rounded/clean corners.
Polyline routing expects segmented non-spline edge paths without illegal node intersections.
Large or dense graphs should remain structurally complete and avoid pathological overlaps.
Edges terminate at rendered shape boundaries rather than node centres.
Simple adjacent-node edges should be direct or softly curved according to configured curve.
Cross-boundary edges should clip to group/member boundaries as applicable and avoid cluster border confusion.
Internal subgraph edges should route within the group while respecting member node bounds.
